claim: Islam et al. (2017) attribute divergent published TRPO/DDPG baseline results directly to under-reported hyperparameters, one year before Henderson et al. (AAAI 2018) formalized the same reality-check lineage.
stance_target: N1: prior work already names unreported implementation choices as the cause of inconsistent published results, predating the specific paper Henderson AAAI 2018
scope_conditions: Continuous control RL, TRPO and DDPG, Hopper and HalfCheetah environments
quoted_support: Our analysis shows that due to the under-reporting of hyper-parameters, different works often report different baseline results and performance measures for both TRPO and DDPG. This leads to an unfair comparison of baselines in continuous control environments.

claim: Islam et al. demonstrate difficulty of fine-tuning hyperparameters causes large variance in reported results, but the paper documents intra-algorithm variance, not a cross-algorithm ranking reversal (which algorithm wins does not flip in this paper).
stance_target: N1 sub-claim (c): a published ranking change is shown when confounds are controlled
quoted_support: We also highlight that there can be difficulty in properly fine-tuning hyper-parameter settings, leading to large variations of reported results across a wide range of works as different hyper-parameters are used.

claim: Islam et al. find HalfCheetah is more susceptible to hyperparameter-driven performance variation than Hopper, attributing the difference to environment dynamics stability -- an environment-dependent confound sensitivity, echoing N1's factor (iii) optimizer/tuning interacting differently by task dimensionality.
stance_target: N1 factor (iii): optimizer tuning effects are task/dimensionality dependent, not uniform
scope_conditions: Hopper vs HalfCheetah MuJoCo continuous control
quoted_support: We find that Half-Cheetah is more susceptible to performance variations from hyper-parameter tuning, while Hopper is not. We posit that this may be due to the difference in stochasticity within the environments themselves.

claim: Islam et al.'s recommendations are reporting guidelines (report hyperparameter ranges, trial counts, all metrics) rather than a single unified corrective protocol with a quantitative before/after decomposition of a headline effect.
stance_target: N1: a formal protocol-plus-eta^2-decomposition shape is owned by this precursor paper
quoted_support: we provide the aforementioned recommendations in reporting implementation details
